docs.title: Health Without Borders — Frontend
docs.text: Flutter cross-platform client for the Health Without Borders initiative.

docs.title: What is this project?
docs.text: Health Without Borders is a mobile and web application designed for vulnerable populations (migrants, rural communities) operating in environments with limited connectivity. The frontend captures medical records in the field using NFC wristbands, stores them locally in SQLite, and automatically synchronizes them with the backend when a connection is available.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
• Offline-first: The synchronization engine runs in the background when a network connection is detected.
  • NFC como identificador: Each patient is linked to an NFC wristband (unique UID). Read/write operations use nfc_manager.
  • Contrato de API estricto: The domain models in lib/src/features/nfc/domain/patient_record.dart are a 1:1 mirror of the backend schemas (FastAPI).
  • Roles y permisos: Access to functionalities is controlled by UserRole (doctor, nurse, org_admin, superadmin).

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text: Layer Technology Framework Flutter 3.41.5 (via FVM) Language Dart 3.8.0 Local Database sqflite (SQLite) NFC nfc_manager 3.5.0 Network HTTP 1.6.0, connectivity_plus Security flutter_secure_storage Voice speech_to_text Platforms iOS, Android, macOS, Web

~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm install 3.41.5

~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter pub get

# 3. Copy environment variables

docs.title: Unit tests (test/unit/)
docs.text:
These tests test pure business logic, without UI. They use repository mocks when necessary.

Recommended pattern:

void main() {
  group('AuthRepository', () {
    late AuthRepository repo;
    late MockApiClient mockClient;

    setUp(() {
      mockClient = MockApiClient();
      repo = AuthRepository(apiClient: mockClient);
    });

    test('login stores token on success', () async {
      when(mockClient.postForm(...)).thenAnswer(
        (_) async => {'access_token': 'fake-token'},
      );
      final session = await repo.login(email: 'a@b.com', password: 'pass');
      expect(session.email, 'a@b.com');
    });
  });
}

docs.title: Widget Tests (test/widget/)
docs.text:
The widget tree is tested using WidgetTester. AppScope with mocked dependencies is used.

Recommended Pattern:

void main() {
  testWidgets('LoginScreen muestra botón de ingreso', (tester) async {
    await tester.pumpWidget(
      MaterialApp(home: LoginScreen()),
    );
    expect(find.text('Ingresar'), findsOneWidget);
  });
}

docs.title: Run a single file
docs.text: ~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter test test/unit/login_unit_test.dart

docs.title: Add new tests
docs.text:
1. Place the file in test/unit/ (logic) or test/widget/ (UI).
  2. Follow the same naming pattern: <name>_test.dart.
  3. Verify that flutter test passes completely before opening the pull request.

NFC in tests

NfcService automatically exports the stub on non-mobile platforms via dart.library.io. The stub is always loaded in the test environment (flutter_test), so it's not necessary to mock the NFC hardware.

docs.title: API and Domain
docs.text:
This section documents the domain models, the HTTP client, and the authentication flow.

  • Domain Models — Dart classes that mirror the backend schema.
  • HTTP Client — ApiClient, error handling, timeouts.
  • Authorization — login, JWT token, roles, and permissions.

docs.title: HTTP Client — ApiClient
docs.text:
lib/src/core/network/api_client.dart

ApiClient is the centralized network layer. All repositories use it; no one calls http.Client directly.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
final apiClient = ApiClient(baseUrl: AppEnv.apiBaseUrl);

baseUrl is read from the environment variable API_BASE_URL defined in .env.

docs.title: postForm — URL-encoded forms
docs.text:
Used for login (OAuth2 form flow):

final data = await apiClient.postForm(
  path: '/api/v1/login/access-token',
  form: {'username': email, 'password': password},
);

docs.title: postJson — JSON body
docs.text:
Used to synchronize patients:

final data = await apiClient.postJson(
  path: '/api/v1/patients/sync',
  body: patientRecord.toJson(),
  headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer $token'},
);

docs.title: getJson — GET with response object
docs.text:
final user = await apiClient.getJson(
  path: '/api/v1/users/me',
  headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer $token'},
);

docs.title: getJsonList — GET with array response
docs.text:
final patients = await apiClient.getJsonList(
  path: '/api/v1/patients',
  headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer $token'},
  queryParams: {'org_id': orgId},
);

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
When the server responds with a code >= 300, ApiClient throws ApiException:

class ApiException implements Exception {
  final String message;
  final int? statusCode;
}

The detail property of the backend JSON response is used as the error message when available.

Example of handling in a repository:

try {
  final data = await apiClient.postJson(...);
  return PatientSyncResponse.fromJson(data);
} on ApiException catch (e) {
  if (e.statusCode == 401) {
    // Expired token — redirect to login
  }
  rethrow;
}

docs.title: Timeout
docs.text: All requests have a 20-second timeout. After this time, http.Client throws a TimeoutException that repositories must catch.

docs.title: HTTP Client Injection (testing)
docs.text:
ApiClient accepts an optional http.Client. This allows a mock to be injected into tests:

final mockClient = MockClient((request) async {
  return http.Response('{"access_token": "fake"}', 200);
});

final apiClient = ApiClient(baseUrl: 'http://test', client: mockClient);

docs.title: Login Flow
docs.text:
LoginScreen
    │
    ▼
AuthRepository.login(email, password)
    │
    ├── POST /api/v1/login/access-token  (form-encoded)
    │       → { access_token: "..." }
    │
    └── GET /api/v1/users/me
            → UserSession { id, email, fullName, role, organizationId }

The JWT token is persisted in FlutterSecureStorage with the key hwb_access_token. On app restart, AuthRepository.getCurrentUser() attempts to retrieve the token and rebuild the session.

docs.title: UserSession
docs.text:
class UserSession {
  final String id;
  final String email;
  final String fullName;
  final UserRole role;
  final String organizationId;
  final String? organizationName;
  final bool isActive;

  String get shortName; // First two words of fullName
}

If the backend does not return full_name, the repository constructs it by humanizing the email: "doctor.juan@org.com" → "Doctor Juan".

docs.title: Roles — UserRole
docs.text:
enum UserRole { superadmin, orgAdmin, doctor, nurse }
Permission doctor nurse orgAdmin superadmin canReadPatients ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ canRegisterPatient ✓ ✓ canAddConsultation ✓ canAddVaccine ✓ ✓ canSyncPatient ✓ ✓ canScanNfc ✓ ✓ canSearchPatient ✓ ✓ ✓ canManageUsers ✓ ✓ canViewAnalytics ✓ ✓

The UI uses these getters directly to show or hide actions:

if (AppScope.of(context).currentUser?.role.canAddConsultation ?? false)
  AddConsultationButton(),

docs.title: Logout
docs.text:
await authRepository.logout();
// Deletes the token from FlutterSecureStorage and clears the session

After logout, the app navigates to the LoginScreen and the SyncEngine must stop.

docs.title: Token Security
docs.text:
• The token is stored exclusively in FlutterSecureStorage — on iOS it uses the Keychain, on Android the Android Keystore.
  • It is Never stored in SharedPreferences or the flat file system.
  • The SyncEngine stops the entire synchronization process upon receiving a 401 error and delegates the re-login to the UI.

docs.title: Domain Models
docs.text:
The models in lib/src/features/nfc/domain/patient_record.dart are a 1:1 mirror of the backend Python schemas (app/schemas/patient.py). Any changes to the backend must be reflected here.

Regulatory reference: Resolutions 866/2021 and 1888/2025 of the Colombian Ministry of Health (RDA — Digital Registry in Care).

docs.title: PatientFullRecord
docs.text:
Root model. This is the body of POST /api/v1/patients/sync and the response of GET /api/v1/patients/scan/{device_uid}.

class PatientFullRecord {
  final String patientId;          // UUID v4 generated by the frontend
  final String deviceUid;          // NFC device UID (hardware)
  final PatientInfo patientInfo;
  final GuardianInfo guardianInfo;
  final BackgroundHistory? backgroundHistory;
  final List<AllergyInfo> allergies;
  final List<MedicalHistoryItem> medicalHistory;
  final List<VaccinationRecordItem> vaccinationRecord;
}

docs.title: PatientInfo
docs.text:
Patient demographics (Elems 1–13 of Res. 866).

Field Type Description identification PatientIdentification Document type and number firstLastName String First surname (Elem. 3.1) secondLastName String? Second surname (Elem. 3.2) firstName String First name (Elem. 3.3) secondName String? Middle name (Elem. 3.4) dob String Date of birth YYYY-MM-DD (Elem. 4) biologicalSex String "M", "F", "I" (Elem. 5) genderIdentity String? "01"–"04", "99" (Elem. 6) ethnicity String? "01"–"06" (Elem. 13.1) nationalityCode String ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, default "COL" address Address Residential Address bloodType String? Blood Type weight / height double? Weight (kg) / Height (cm)

Supported Document Types: CC, CE, PA, RC, TI, SC, PE, PT, MS, AS, CN, DE.

docs.title: GuardianInfo
docs.text:
Patient's Guardian or Caregiver.

class GuardianInfo {
  final String name;
  final String relationship;
  final String phone;
  final String? deviceUid;   // Guardian's NFC device UID
}

docs.title: BackgroundHistory
docs.text:
Personal and Family History.

class BackgroundHistory {
  final String? chronicConditions;       // Chronic conditions (free text)
  final String? personalHistory;         // Personal history (free text)
  final List<FamilyHistoryItem> familyHistory;
  final String? familyHistoryNotes;
}

docs.title: FamilyHistoryItem
docs.text:
The frontend sends conditionDescription (free text) and relationship. The backend resolves the ICD-10 and ICD-11 codes using LLM.

Code relationship Meaning "01" Parents "02" Brothers "03" Aunts/Uncles "04" Grandparents

docs.title: AllergyInfo
docs.text:
Res. 866, Elems. 47.1 y 47.2.

Code category Meaning "01" Medication "02" Food "03" Environmental Substance "04" Substance on Skin "05" Insect Bite "06" Other

docs.title: VaccinationRecordItem
docs.text:
class VaccinationRecordItem {
  final String date;             // YYYY-MM-DD
  final String vaccineName;
  final String vaccineCode;      // CVX Code
  final int dose;
  final String administratedBy;
  final String administratedAt;
  final String status;           // "completed" by default
}

docs.title: MedicalHistoryItem
docs.text:
A clinical query (RDA-Query, Res. 866).

The diagnosis and riskFactors fields are sent as empty lists from the frontend; the backend resolves them using LLM based on clinicalEvaluation.

Key Fields:

Field Values ​​ careModality "01"–"09" serviceGroup "01"–"05" careEnvironment "01"–"05" diagnosisType "01" Confirmed, "02" Presumptive, "03" Discarded dischargeDisposition "01"–"04"

docs.title: PatientSyncResponse
docs.text:
Response from POST /api/v1/patients/sync:

class PatientSyncResponse {
  final String status;       // "success" or "error"
  final String internalId;   // Internal backend ID
  final String? fhirStatus;  // FHIR integration status
  final String? vidaCode;    // VIDA code (national system)
  final String message;
}

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
This section describes how the code is organized, what each layer does, and how data flows from NFC capture to synchronization with the backend.

  • Project Structure — directory tree and conventions.
  • Modules and Features — description of each feature in lib/src/features/.
  • Offline-First and Synchronization — local data flow → backend.
  • NFC Encryption and Key Ring — wire format, key ring, session window and build compatibility.

docs.title: Modules and Features
docs.text: Each feature resides in lib/src/features/<name>/. This page describes what each feature does and what screens it exposes.

docs.title: auth — Authentication
docs.text:
Manages the user session lifecycle.

Screens:

  • login_screen.dart — email/password form. Calls POST /api/v1/login/access-token (form-encoded) and then GET /api/v1/users/me to retrieve the user profile.

Domain:

  • UserSession — represents the authenticated user with their role, organization, and name.

  • UserRole — enum with four roles: doctor, nurse, orgAdmin, superadmin. Each role exposes boolean getters (canReadPatients, canAddConsultation, etc.) that the UI consumes directly.

Repositories:

  • AuthRepository — login, logout, and JWT token management in FlutterSecureStorage.
  • UserRepository — retrieves the authenticated user's profile from the backend.

docs.title: nfc — Patients and NFC
docs.text:
Main feature of the app. It centralizes all the logic for capturing and displaying clinical data.

Main Flow:

  1. NFC Read (read_nfc_screen.dart) — scans the wristband and obtains the device UID.
  2. Registration (register/register_nfc_screen.dart) — a 6-step wizard to register a new patient.
  3. Profile (profile/patient_profile_screen.dart) — view of the medical record tabs.
  4. Lost Wristband (loss_of_wristband_screen.dart) — search for a patient by name/document.

Editing Screens (sheets):

  • add_consultation_screen.dart / add_vaccine_screen.dart — add clinical entries.
  • Sheets in profile/sheets/ — inline editing of allergies, family history, vital signs, address, and guardian.

Profile Tabs:

Tab File Content Summary profile_tab_summary.dart Demographics, vital signs Background profile_tab_background.dart Chronic conditions, family history Allergies profile_tab_allergies.dart List of allergies with category and reaction Vaccinations profile_tab_vaccines.dart Vaccination history Consultations profile_tab_consultations.dart Medical consultation history

docs.title: home — Home screen
docs.text:
home_screen.dart displays the actions available based on the user's role:

  • Doctor / Nurse: Scan NFC, Register patient, Sync queue.
  • Org Admin: Brigade statistics, Manage users/organizations.

Screens visible only to orgAdmin and superadmin:

  • brigade_stats_screen.dart — Brigade KPIs and statistics.
  • manage_users_screen.dart — User list and creation.
  • manage_organizations_screen.dart — Organization management.

docs.title: NFC encryption and the key ring
docs.text:
How the app encrypts what it writes to NFC chips, which key it uses, and why a reader sometimes refuses a chip it can physically see.

The operational side — generating keys, rotating, retiring, and the rules that silently destroy chip readability if broken — lives in the backend runbook: NFC Key Management. Read it before touching anything to do with keys in a deployed environment.

docs.title: What is on the chip
docs.text:
Every HWB chip — a patient bracelet or a guardian card — carries its clinical payload through this pipeline:

JSON map → CBOR → DEFLATE → AES-256-GCM

lib/src/core/nfc/nfc_payload_codec.dart owns all of it. Both chip types go through the same NfcPayloadService and therefore the same key.

The chip's hardware UID is not encrypted and is always readable. That matters: a device with connectivity can resolve the patient from the UID alone through /patients/scan, even when it cannot decrypt the payload. The chip is a cache for offline use; the backend is the source of truth.

docs.title: Wire format
docs.text:
version 0 : [12-byte nonce][ciphertext][16-byte auth tag]
version 1+: ['H']['W'][version][nonce][ciphertext][tag]

For version 1 and above, the three header bytes are passed to AES-GCM as associated data, so the version byte cannot be stripped or edited without failing authentication.

Version 0 deliberately writes no header. This is not an oversight. A build that predates key versioning reads the first bytes as the nonce, so a header there would make everything written by a newer build unreadable to an older one — during any partial rollout, which is the normal state of a device fleet. A header only ever appears once a deployment rotates to version 1.

decode() reads both layouts. For a headerless payload it reports the version whose key succeeded, which is the version the chip is effectively on.

docs.title: The key ring, not a key
docs.text:
The backend delivers a ring — version -> key — at login, refresh and /users/me. NfcKeyring (lib/src/core/nfc/nfc_keyring.dart) holds it; AuthRepository.getNfcKeyring() is the single accessor.

Reads resolve whichever version the chip names. Writes use the ring's current version.

Always build the codec from the ring

NfcPayloadCodec(hexKey: ...) stamps version 0 into the header while encrypting with whatever key it was handed. After a rotation that produces a chip no reader can decrypt — silently and permanently. This is not hypothetical: it is a defect that reached develop once and had to be fixed. Use NfcPayloadCodec.fromKeyring(keyring: ...).

A malformed key in the ring is dropped with a log line rather than rejected wholesale, so one bad key delivered by the backend degrades that version instead of disabling NFC entirely. If the dropped version happens to be the current one, the codec becomes read-only: it refuses to write rather than encrypt with a guessed key.

docs.title: The session window
docs.text:
The ring is only served while the refresh token's exp is still in the future. The claim is read locally from the JWT, so the check works with no connectivity — which is the point.

Outside the window the ring is wiped from memory and from disk, and NFC reads and writes are refused. The session itself is still restored, because the device may hold unsynced records the health worker needs to see; what appears is the persistent SessionWindowBanner telling them to reconnect.

The window slides forward on every successful refresh, so someone using the app normally never meets it. Reaching it requires roughly a week with no connectivity at all.

docs.title: Clock handling
docs.text:
The window is judged against the device clock, so a stored high-water mark (hwb_clock_mark) detects the clock being moved backwards: more than 24 hours behind the mark closes the window. The tolerance absorbs NTP corrections and timezone changes.

The mark is re-anchored to the server's clock — the refresh token's iat — on every successful login and refresh. Without that, a device whose clock ran ahead even briefly would keep a mark in the future and refuse NFC until real time caught up, with no way out but clearing app storage, which destroys pending records.

docs.title: Key version telemetry
docs.text:
Every chip read records which key version opened it, keyed by device UID in nfc_key_version_observations, with a patient / guardian role. SyncEngine ships pending observations and marks them reported only after the server confirms.

This exists for one operational question: can a key version be retired without leaving chips unreadable offline? A chip carries no readable hint of its version, so measuring is the only way to know how far a rotation has drained.

observed_at is stored and sent in UTC. A naive local timestamp is read by the server as UTC and shifts every sighting by the device's offset.

The whole path is best-effort: every failure is caught and logged. A lost observation delays a rotation decision; a broken read leaves a clinician with no history in front of a patient. Those are not comparable, and the code treats them accordingly.

docs.title: Updating the fleet
docs.text:
The build compatibility rule that matters, in both directions:

Chip written by Read by older build Read by current build Older build (no versioning) ✅ ✅ Current build, version 0 ✅ ✅ Current build, version 1+ ❌ ✅

So while NFC_CURRENT_KEY_VERSION is 0, builds are interchangeable in both directions and a partial rollout is safe.

Before any rotation

NFC_CURRENT_KEY_VERSION must stay at 0 until every device runs a build that understands the ring. An older build takes the current key, ignores the ring, and loses the ability to read everything written under version 0. Confirm the fleet first; the backend runbook has the procedure.

As of the current build, no rotation has occurred: every chip in the field is version 0, headerless.

docs.title: Offline-first and synchronization
docs.text: The app is designed to work without an internet connection. This page explains how data is stored locally and how it is synchronized with the backend when a network connection is available.

docs.title: Local storage — LocalDatabase
docs.text:
lib/src/core/storage/local_database.dart is a singleton that wraps sqflite.

Schema of the local_patients table:

CREATE TABLE local_patients (
  patient_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, -- UUID v4 generated by the frontend
  device_uid TEXT NOT NULL, -- NFC wristband UID
  patient_name TEXT NOT NULL, -- Name to display in the UI
  record_json TEXT NOT NULL, -- PatientFullRecord serialized as JSON
  is_synced INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- 0 = pending, 1 = synchronized
  sync_error TEXT, -- Message of the last sync error
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL, -- ISO 8601
  synced_at TEXT -- ISO 8601 — null until the first successful sync
)

Almacenamiento en Web

sqflite is not available in Flutter Web. LocalDatabase uses a localStorage-backed store as its persistence layer on Web, not just a development fallback — it is the production storage path for this platform. Clinical payloads (record_json) are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being written, the index patient_name column is masked (e.g. "Ana G.") rather than stored in full, and the break-glass emergency log encrypts patient_name/user_id the same way. See web/index.html's Content-Security-Policy for the defense-in-depth layer that protects this storage against script-injection exfiltration.

docs.title: Synchronization Engine — SyncEngine
docs.text: lib/src/core/sync/sync_engine.dart implements the background synchronization cycle.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
// Start connectivity monitoring
syncEngine.start();

// Stop (example, on logout)
syncEngine.stop();

docs.title: Synchronization Flow
docs.text:
Connectivity Detected
        │
        ▼
getUnsyncedRecords()   ← list local_patients WHERE is_synced = 0
        │
        ▼ (for each record)
POST /api/v1/patients/sync
        │
   ┌────┴────┐
   │  201    │  → markSynced(patientId)   → scrub of clinical data
   │  4xx    │  → markSyncError(message)  → hold for review
   │  5xx    │  → markSyncError(message)  → automatic retry
   │  401    │  → detener sync            → redirect to login
   └─────────┘

docs.title: Behavior by Error Code
docs.text: Code Action 201 Marks as synchronized, deletes clinical data from the local record 400 / 422 Does not retry — data error, user should review 401 Stops synchronization entirely — token expired, requires re-login 429 / 500 Keeps is_synced = 0 for automatic retry Timeout Keeps is_synced = 0 for automatic retry

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text:
syncEngine.onSyncStatusChanged = (int unsyncedCount) {
  // Update badge/counter in the UI
};

syncEngine.onRecordSynced = (String patientId, bool success, String? error) {
  // React to the synchronization of a specific record
};

docs.title: Scrubbing of Clinical Data
docs.text:
Once a record is successfully synchronized with the backend, the app removes the clinical data from local storage (the record_json field) for security reasons. It only retains the metadata: patient_id, device_uid, patient_name, is_synced, synced_at.

This protects patient privacy in case of device loss or theft.

docs.title: Connectivity
docs.text: lib/src/core/network/connectivity_service uses connectivity_plus to detect network changes (WiFi, mobile data). The SyncEngine subscribes to these events and automatically calls syncAll() upon regaining a connection.

docs.title: Naming conventions
docs.text:
• Files: snake_case for everything (Dart files, directories, assets).
  • Clases: PascalCase.
  • Features: Each feature resides in its own directory with subfolders data/, domain/, and presentation/ where applicable.
  • Screen widgets: _screen.dart suffix for full screens, _sheet.dart for bottom sheets.

docs.title: Dependency Injection
docs.text:
The project uses AppScope (an InheritedWidget) instead of an external DI package. All dependencies are instantiated in main.dart and passed down through the widget tree:

AppScope(
  authRepository: authRepo,
  userRepository: userRepo,
  patientRepository: patientRepo,
  localDatabase: LocalDatabase.instance,
  syncEngine: syncEngine,
  child: const MyApp(),
)

To access a dependency from any widget:

final scope = AppScope.of(context);
final user = scope.currentUser;

docs.title: DPG Compliance Checklist — Health Without Borders (Frontend / Flutter client)
docs.text:
Health Without Borders ships as two repositories — a FastAPI backend and this Flutter client — that are assessed against the Digital Public Goods Standard separately, because several indicators land on one side only (e.g. the API is what exposes non-PII data; the client is what encrypts data at rest on the device). This checklist scores each of the nine indicators as they apply to this repository specifically; where the underlying mechanism actually lives in the backend, the note says so and points there instead of this repo claiming credit for work it doesn't do.

  • Status legend: ✅ Met · 🟡 Partial · 🔴 Gap
# DPG Standard indicator Status What this repo actually does 1 Relevance to the SDGs (SDG 3 — Health) ✅ Met This is the field tool brigades use: NFC-based patient registration, offline consultations/vaccines, and guardian consent capture for migrant and pediatric populations. 2 Use of an approved open license ✅ Met MIT (LICENSE), independent of the backend's own licensing. 3 Clear ownership ✅ Met PROJECT_CHARTER.md names guane emerging technologies as owner and lays out the trademark policy for "Health Without Borders" / "HWB" separately from the code license. 4 Platform independence ✅ Met One Flutter codebase ships to iOS, Android, macOS, Linux, Windows and Web (pubspec.yaml, per-platform runners in the repo). The only hard platform dependency is NFC hardware itself, which is inherent to the feature, not a vendor lock-in — the web build falls back to a no-op NFC stub (nfc_service_stub.dart) rather than failing. 5 Documentation ✅ Met MkDocs site (mkdocs.yml) covers local setup, project structure, offline-sync design, and the domain-model contract with the backend — published from docs/. 6 Mechanism for extracting non-PII data 🟡 Partial The actual extraction mechanism (the aggregated stats API) lives in the backend repo, not here. This repo only surfaces it: StatsRepository calls it and the brigade-metrics screen renders it. Marked Partial rather than Met because this repository, on its own, doesn't expose the data — it depends on the backend being deployed and reachable. 7 Adherence to privacy & applicable laws ✅ Met Guardian consent is captured and stored per Ley 1581/2012 (GuardianConsent, signature capture); Android's data_extraction_rules.xml explicitly excludes app data from cloud backup and device-transfer so PHI never leaves the device outside the app's own sync path. 8 Adherence to standards & best practices ✅ Met patient_record.dart mirrors the backend's FHIR R4 / RDA schemas field-for-field so the two repos can't silently drift; flutter analyze + flutter test + coverage gate every PR (ci.yml, cloudbuild.pr.yaml). 9a Do No Harm — Data Privacy & Security ✅ Met This is where the client carries the most weight: local SQLite is AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest (LocalDatabase), NFC wristband/card payloads are separately AES-256-GCM encrypted with per-org keys (NfcPayloadCodec), auth tokens sit in OS-level secure storage, UI is gated by role (UserRole), and any guardian-absent "emergency access" view is logged locally and synced for audit (logEmergencyAccess). 9b Do No Harm — Inappropriate & Illegal Content 🟡 Partial There's no open posting surface — the only free-text is clinician-entered clinical notes (optionally via speech-to-text). Still open: a one-line statement in the docs saying this explicitly, so it's not just implicit from reading the code. 9c Do No Harm — Protection from Harassment ✅ Met Same CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and enforcement contact as the backend; this repo has no separate community space, so nothing extra to moderate here.

docs.title: Action plan for open gaps
docs.text:
• [ ] Add a short "no user-generated content" note to docs/ covering the clinical free-text/voice-dictation fields. (indicator 9b)
  • [ ] Cross-link this checklist and the backend's checklist for indicator 6, so a reader of either one knows the extraction mechanism itself is documented on the backend side.
  • [ ] Have the privacy & security mentor review indicator 7 and 9a specifically against data_extraction_rules.xml, NfcPayloadCodec, and LocalDatabase's key-handling.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: This section covers everything you need to contribute to the frontend: from setting up your local environment to successfully opening a pull request.

docs.title: Development Stack
docs.text:
Tool Version Purpose Flutter 3.41.5 Cross-platform UI framework Dart SDK ^3.11.3 Language (included with Flutter) flutter_lints ^6.0.0 Linting rules flutter_test SDK Testing suite

Production dependencies (NFC, SQLite, HTTP, etc.) are declared in pubspec.yaml. Do not install versions other than those specified there—the app is sensitive to API changes between minor versions of nfc_manager and sqflite.

docs.title: Standard Workflow
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and start the environment → setup.md
2. Create the feat/<name> branch from develop
3. Develop with Flutter Analyze running in watch mode
4. Write or update tests in test/unit/ or test/widget/
5. Implement local quality gates → qa-plan.md
6. Open a pull request against develop using the template → qa-plan.md

docs.title: Recommended Environment
docs.text:
VS Code with the following extensions:

  • Flutter — autocompletion, hot reload, debugging.
  • Dart — real-time static analysis.

Add this to .vscode/settings.json so that VS Code uses the correct Flutter SDK:

{
  "dart.flutterSdkPath": ".fvm/flutter_sdk"
}

Android Studio / IntelliJ also work with the official Flutter plugin.

docs.title: Everyday Commands
docs.text:
# Install dependencies after a git pull
flutter pub get

# Hot reload (within a session `flutter run`)
r

# Static analysis
flutter analyze

# Run all tests
flutter test

# Run a specific test
flutter test test/unit/login_unit_test.dart

# View available devices
flutter devices

# Clean up build artifacts (useful when there are unusual errors)
flutter clean && flutter pub get

docs.title: Detailed Guides
docs.text:
• Local Configuration — prerequisites, Flutter installation, environment variables, and platform-specific configuration.
  • QA and PR Flow — quality gates, branch policy, PR template, and CI pipeline descriptions.
  • Figma to Flutter — how to translate layouts to widgets, layout tokens, and existing shared widgets.

docs.title: Design Source of Truth
docs.text: Figma is the source of truth for all visual designs. Flutter code is the implementation; Figma design is the specification.

docs.title: Design Tokens
docs.text:
Design tokens are centralized in:

  • lib/src/design/tokens/app_colors.dart — color palette.

  • lib/src/design/theme/app_theme.dart — ThemeData configuration.

When deploying a new component, always use tokens instead of hardcoded values:

// ✅ Correct
color: AppColors.primary,
style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.bodyLarge,

// ❌ Incorrect
color: Color(0xFF00897B),
fontSize: 16,

docs.title: Flujo de implementación recomendado
docs.text:
1. Extract tokens in Figma Dev Mode — colors, font, spacing, borders.
  2. Update app_colors.dart and app_theme.dart if there are new values.
  3. Build atomic widgets first — buttons (HwbButton), inputs (HwbTextField), logo (HwbLogo) before screens.
  4. Implement the screen using existing widgets and theme tokens.
  5. Validate on multiple sizes — use the MediaQuery widget and test on at least two screen sizes (small phone and tablet).

docs.title: Sheets and modals
docs.text:
The project uses bottom sheets extensively for inline editing. The standard structure is:

showModalBottomSheet(
  context: context,
  isScrollControlled: true,
  builder: (_) => SheetScaffold(
    title: 'Título del sheet',

docs.title: Using Figma MCP
docs.text: If you have Figma's MCP set up in your environment, you can provide a Figma URL and node ID to extract the design context directly and translate it into Flutter components aligned with the conventions of this repository.

docs.title: Local Quality Gates
docs.text:
Run the following commands before opening any PR. CI will run them automatically, but it's faster to detect issues locally.

# Static Dart Analysis
~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter analyze

# Full Test Suite
~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter test

Both should pass without errors or new warnings.

docs.title: Branch Policy
docs.text:
Branch Purpose main Production and stable code. PRs only from develop. develop Integration branch. Feature PRs go here. feat/<nombre> Individual feature branches.

Normal Flow:

feat/my-feature → develop → main

Always open pull requests against develop. Only the lead team merges develop into main.

docs.title: Pull Request Template
docs.text:
Use the template in .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Include:

  • Description of the change and its motivation.
  • Screenshots or video if there are visual changes.
  • Testing checklist (unit, widget, manual on physical device).
  • Reference to the Jira/Linear issue or task.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text: The repository has two pipelines:

docs.title: docs.yml — Documentation Publish
docs.text: This pipeline runs on every push to main or develop, and manually from Actions. Deploy this documentation to GitHub Pages using MkDocs Material.

docs.title: ci.yml — Quality gates (manual backup)
docs.text: Backup pipeline that executes flutter analyze and flutter test. Currently, it is manually triggered (workflow_dispatch). The main CI/CD pipeline runs on Cloud Build (GCP).

docs.title: Test Coverage
docs.text:
The current suite covers:

  • test/unit/login_unit_test.dart — login logic and session parsing.
  • test/unit/home_screen_test.dart — initial state of the home screen.
  • test/unit/porfile_tab_summary_test.dart — profile summary tab logic.
  • test/widget/login_widget_test.dart — login form rendering.
  • test/widget/home_screen_widget_test.dart — home widget tree.
  • test/widget/porfile_tab_summary_widget_test.dart — Summary tab rendering.

To add tests, follow the existing structure and place the files in test/unit/ or test/widget/ as appropriate.

docs.title: Linting
docs.text: Analysis rules are in analysis_options.yaml, which extends flutter_lints. Avoid silencing warnings with // ignore: without documented justification in the same comment.

docs.text: Tool Required Version Notes Flutter (via FVM) 3.41.5 Do not install Flutter directly — use FVM Dart SDK 3.8.0 Included with Flutter 3.41.5 Xcode 15+ For iOS/macOS builds only Android Studio Ladybug+ For Android builds and the emulator Android SDK API 21+ Minimum supported level

docs.title: Install FVM and Flutter
docs.text:
FVM (Flutter Version Management) allows you to fix the SDK version per project, ensuring that all team members use the exact same version.

# Activate FVM globally
dart pub global activate fvm

# Install the project version
~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm install 3.41.5

# Set the version in the repository directory
~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm use 3.41.5

The .fvmrc file in the repository root already contains the correct version. FVM will automatically read it from the project directory.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
The app uses flutter_dotenv to load runtime configuration.

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env with the values ​​corresponding to your environment:

# Base URL of the backend (without trailing slash)
API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000

# Production example
# API_BASE_URL=https://api.healthwithoutborders.org

.env files and assets

The .env and .env.production files are declared as assets in pubspec.yaml. Do not delete them — the app loads them in main.dart via flutter_dotenv.

docs.title: Install dependencies
docs.text: ~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter pub get

docs.title: Run the application
docs.text:
macOSAndroidiOSWeb (Chrome) 
~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter run -d macos

# List available devices/emulators
~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter devices

~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter run -d <device-id>

# Requires Xcode and a simulator or physical device
~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter run -d iPhone

~/.pub-cache/bin/fvm flutter run -d chrome

NFC on web

NFC reading is not available in browsers. On the web, the NfcService uses the stub (nfc_service_stub.dart) that simulates the operation.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text:
This guide is for the healthcare staff who use the Health Without Borders mobile app in the field — during medical brigades and at pilot sites. It explains, step by step, how to register patients, read and update their records with NFC/QR bracelets, and keep everything synchronized.

No technical knowledge is required. If you are looking for API, architecture, or deployment documentation, see the Development and Infrastructure and Security sections instead.

docs.title: What the app does
docs.text:
Health Without Borders stores a patient's clinical record on an NFC/QR bracelet and keeps a synchronized copy on the server. Because brigades often work without a stable internet connection, the app is offline-first: you can register patients and record care with no signal, and the app will synchronize automatically when a connection is available.

A single patient has one shared record across all participating organizations, so any authenticated professional can read and update it at the point of care.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A mobile device with NFC enabled (Android) and the app installed.
  • Your login credentials, provided by your organization administrator.
  • Patient NFC bracelets and, when applicable, guardian cards.

Note: The interface is available in Spanish and English. You can switch the language at any time from the header (see Getting Started).

docs.title: How this guide is organized
docs.text:
1. Getting Started — Log in, understand the home screen, switch language, and sign out safely.
  2. Registering a New Patient — Create a patient, assign the bracelet, and add guardians.
  3. Finding & Viewing a Patient — Search, scan a bracelet, and read the clinical history.
  4. Consultations & Vaccines — Add care to a patient's record.
  5. Syncing Pending Records — Understand and clear the sync queue.
  6. Statistics — Review brigade activity (administrators).
  7. Administration — Manage users and organizations (administrators).

docs.title: Administration: Users & Organizations
docs.text: These screens are for administrators. They let you manage the people and organizations that use the platform.

docs.title: 1. Manage users
docs.text:
Open Manage users to see the users in your organization, grouped by role (for example, Administrator, Doctor, Nurse).

From a user's detail you can:

  • Create a new user.
  • Deactivate a user — the account is suspended but not removed.
  • Delete a user — the account is removed.

docs.title: 2. Manage organizations
docs.text:
Open Organizations to see the list of organizations. Selecting one opens its details (identifier, status, number of users, number of patients).

From an organization's detail you can:

  • Deactivate the organization.
  • Delete the organization.

Note: Deleting an organization protects patient records — patient data is never removed. Associated user accounts are deactivated together with the organization.

docs.title: 3. A note on roles
docs.text: What you can see and do depends on your role. Organization administrators act within their own organization; super administrators can act across organizations. If an option is not visible to you, your role does not include that permission.

docs.title: Consultations & Vaccines
docs.text: This page explains how to add clinical care — consultations and vaccines — to a patient's record.

docs.title: 1. Add a consultation
docs.text:
1. Open the patient's record (by scanning the bracelet or searching), or use the summary screen right after registration.
  2. Tap Add consultation.
  3. Complete the consultation details and save.

docs.title: 2. Add a vaccine
docs.text:
1. From the same summary or record screen, tap Add vaccine.
  2. Enter the vaccine information and save.

docs.title: 3. How the bracelet is updated
docs.text:
When you add a consultation or a vaccine, the bracelet is marked as modified so the new information is written back to the NFC chip and synchronized to the server. If you are offline, the change is stored locally and appears in the pending-to-sync queue until a connection is available.

Note: After adding care, use Finish to complete the encounter. Remember to write the bracelet if it is still marked as pending.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This page covers logging in, the home screen, changing the language, and signing out safely.

docs.title: 1. Logging in
docs.text:
1. Open the app. On the login screen, enter the email and password provided by your organization administrator.
  2. Tap Log in.

Your access depends on your role (for example, medical staff, or an organization administrator). Administrators see additional options such as Statistics, Manage users, and Organizations.

Note: Once you are logged in, the app keeps your session active as you move between screens. If your session expires, you will be asked to sign in again — any records you registered in the field are kept on the device until they can be synchronized.

docs.title: 2. The home screen
docs.text:
From the home screen you can reach the main actions:

  • New patient — register a patient and assign a bracelet.
  • Search patients — find an existing patient.
  • Pending to sync — review records waiting to be uploaded. A gold badge shows the number of records still stored locally (including any duplicates or errors).

Administrators also see Statistics, Manage users, and Organizations.

docs.title: 3. Changing the language
docs.text:
The app is bilingual. Use the ES / EN switch in the header to change the language instantly — titles, buttons, filters, and cards update immediately, with no need to restart the screen. Dates are also shown in the format that matches the selected language.

The language switch is available on the main screens, including New patient, Search patients, Pending to sync, Manage users, and Organizations.

docs.title: Finding & Viewing a Patient
docs.text: This page explains how to find an existing patient and how to read a patient's clinical record from their bracelet.

docs.title: 1. Search for a patient
docs.text:
1. From the home screen, tap Search patients.
  2. Enter the patient's identifying details (for example, document number or name).
  3. Tap Search.

If no match is found, the app shows the message: "No patient found with these details. Please check the fields." Review the values you entered and try again.

docs.title: 2. Read a patient by scanning the bracelet
docs.text:
At the point of care, the fastest way to open a record is to scan the patient's bracelet:

  1. Choose the read option and tap Start.
  2. Hold the patient's bracelet (or the guardian card) against the back of the phone.
  3. The patient's record opens once the bracelet is read.

Note: The bracelet identifier is unambiguous, so scanning always opens the correct patient. Manual search is best when the bracelet is unavailable.

docs.title: 3. Read the clinical record
docs.text:
When a record is open, the information is organized into tabs:

  • Summary — the patient's key information at a glance.
  • Consultations — the list of recorded consultations.
  • Vaccines — the vaccines registered for the patient.
  • Consultation details — the full detail of a selected consultation.

Dates are shown in the format that matches the selected language (ES / EN).

docs.title: 4. Emergency access
docs.text: In urgent situations, the app provides an emergency ("break-glass") access path so that care is never blocked. Every emergency access is recorded in an audit log (who accessed the record and when). Use it only when clinically necessary.

docs.title: Registering a New Patient
docs.text: This page explains how to create a new patient, assign the patient's NFC bracelet, and add one or two guardians.

docs.title: 1. Start a new registration
docs.text:
1. From the home screen, tap New patient.
  2. The registration form opens. You can switch the language (ES / EN) at any time from the header.

docs.title: 2. Enter the patient's information
docs.text:
Complete the fields in each section:

  • Patient NFC device — the identifier of the bracelet you will assign (you can also scan it in the next step).
  • Identification — document type, document number, first and last names (second name and second surname are optional).
  • Demographic data — date of birth and biological sex.
  • Nationality — choose from the list. If the nationality is not listed, select "Other".

Required fields are marked with an asterisk (). The Continue* button advances through the steps.

docs.title: 3. Assign the patient bracelet
docs.text:
When prompted, the app shows the guided writing screen ("Patient bracelet"):

  1. Tap Start.
  2. Hold the patient's bracelet against the back of the phone until the app confirms the write.

Note: You can tap Skip to finish the registration without writing the bracelet immediately. In that case the patient is saved locally and marked as "Pending to write to the NFC device", so you can write the bracelet later.

docs.title: 4. Add guardians
docs.text:
For patients who require a guardian, you can register up to two guardians:

  1. Enter each guardian's information.
  2. Capture the guardian's consent signature when requested.
  3. When prompted with the "Guardian card" screen, hold the guardian card against the phone to write it.

Note: The guardian's consent signature is preserved on the server; it is not lost when the guardian card is synchronized.

docs.title: 5. Finish and save
docs.text:
On the summary screen you can:

  • Add consultation or Add vaccine (see Consultations & Vaccines).
  • Tap Finish to complete the registration.

The patient is saved locally first and appears in the pending-to-sync queue until the app uploads it to the server.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text: The Statistics screen gives administrators an overview of brigade activity — patients, vaccines, and nationalities. Availability depends on your role.

docs.title: 1. Access and scope
docs.text:
• Organization administrators see the statistics for their own organization.
  • Super administrators can see all organizations, or narrow the view to a single one using the organization dropdown.

You can switch the language (ES / EN) from the header.

docs.title: 2. Filter by period
docs.text:
Use the quick filter buttons to choose the time window:

  • All — all available data.
  • This month — the current month to date.
  • Last 20 days — a rolling recent window.
  • Custom — opens a calendar where you select a specific date range.

The figures and trends update to match the selected period, comparing it against the previous one where applicable.

docs.title: Syncing Pending Records
docs.text: Because the app is offline-first, records you create in the field are first saved on the device and then uploaded to the server. This page explains how to review and clear those pending records.

docs.title: 1. Why records are pending
docs.text: When there is no connection — or when a bracelet still needs to be written — new patients and updates are stored locally and queued for synchronization. The home screen shows a gold badge with the number of records still pending (including any duplicates or records with errors).

docs.title: 2. The sync queue
docs.text:
Open Pending to sync from the home screen. Each record is shown as a card with a clear status:

  • Pending — waiting to be uploaded.
  • Error — the upload did not complete; the card explains, in plain language, what to do.
  • Duplicate — the record matches one already on the server.

docs.title: 3. Synchronize
docs.text:
• Tap Sync now on a single record, or Sync all to upload the whole queue.
  • Tap Review to inspect a record before syncing.

When a record uploads successfully, it leaves the queue and the home badge count goes down.

Note: Technical system-error details are intentionally hidden from this screen to keep it clear. When you sign out, the app warns you if records are still pending — sync them first whenever possible so nothing is left only on the device.
